newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes weaker as current a/c trumps RBNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes weaker as current a/c trumps RBNZ.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed weaker as markets bucked warnings from the Reserve Bank and took their cue from a worse-than-expected current account deficit.
The kiwi ended Friday at US$0.6694/01, down from its 0.6721/28 opening, with the Trade Weighted Index at 65.81, down from its 66.02 local opening.
"The current account was the morning focus and the afternoon the RB's statement," an Auckland-based bank dealer said.

The March year current account deficit, equating to a weaker than expected 4.8 percent of GDP, saw the dollar dip sharply, but rise again briefly when the Reserve Bank said monetary conditions had eased too far.

"The thing that is most interesting on the day is one, the (current account) number is appalling, and the other is that the market is not taking the RB's wish on board about monetary conditions," the dealer said.

"I think the currency is basically quite weak and if there is going to be a tightening it will have to come via the interest rates, but those guys seem to be pretty hung up on the CPI next week. So they are in quite a difficult position, the RB, right now."
He said the problem facing the RBNZ was a timing one. While it wanted an easing towards the end of the year the market was keen to have one now.
A Wellington bank dealer said the kiwi had closed "fairly anaemic close" with a fairly muted response to the RBNZ's comments.

"The local market is long basically and there has been fairly aggressive selling in the last three days from an offshore party, so whilst the locals will take on board what (RBNZ Governor) Don Brash says, basically they have got no choice. Too much is being sold into it," he said.
"At some point it is going to become self-fulfilling, that there will be investor demand to offset the selling, but at the moment it is all supply."
Dealers said the kiwi should find a base between 0.6680 and 0.6685 overnight and trade up to 20 or 25 basis points above the 0.67 figure.
"I actually quite like kiwi down here. Around 0.6680 should be a base for it. I think 0.6685/20 overnight," the Wellington dealer said.
